title: INNIO books 450 MW firm order for Jenbacher J624 gas engines for US data-centre prime power
description: INNIO announced a 450 MW order from an undisclosed US energy company for containerized Jenbacher J624 gas engines to support behind-the-meter prime power for large-scale data centres in North America. The order was booked in Q3 2026 and the engines are expected to be delivered by 2028.
quote: data center developers are seeking on-site and behind-the-meter power solutions that can be delivered independently of the growing grid constraints in North America
analysis: Gas-engine prime power for data centres is being booked years ahead (delivery by 2028), which signals tight engine and container supply that Gulf data-centre buyers will also compete for. Action: confirm with Cummins which 2027-28 gas genset production slots can be reserved for Gulf data-centre bids before quoting delivery dates.

title: HD Construction Equipment signs KRW 390 billion deal to supply gas engines for US hyperscale data-centre gensets
description: South Korea's HD Construction Equipment signed a 390 billion won (USD 291.4 million) agreement with US firm ERock to supply 22-liter long-block gas engines from 2027 through 2028. ERock will build them into generator sets for hyperscale data centres run by US tech companies.
quote: ERock will integrate the partially assembled engines into generator sets to supply power to hyperscale data centers operated by US tech companies
analysis: A new Asian engine maker is entering the data-centre genset supply chain for 2027-28, which adds engine supply but also a new low-cost engine brand that could later reach Gulf packagers. Action: add HD Construction Equipment / ERock to the competitor watchlist and check whether they plan any Middle East channel.

title: Cushman & Wakefield: Americas data-centre construction hits a record 37.7 GW, 91.7% precommitted, vacancy 3.8%
description: Cushman & Wakefield's H1 2026 Americas Data Center Update reports a record 37.7 GW under construction, with 50.3 GW operational and another 285 GW in the planned pipeline. Vacancy has fallen to 3.8% and access to power and infrastructure is increasingly determining where growth can occur.
quote: Capacity under construction is 91.7 percent precommitted, while region-wide vacancy has fallen to just 3.8 percent
analysis: Near-fully precommitted construction shows sustained global demand for backup and prime power, which supports Cummins' order book but also means US projects absorb large-genset production that Gulf projects need. Action: ask Cummins for allocation visibility on 2.5 MW+ gensets for pending Gulf data-centre awards.

title: JLL: Asia-Pacific data-centre capacity to nearly double from 32 GW to 57 GW by 2030, grid connections a bottleneck
description: JLL expects Asia-Pacific data-centre capacity to rise from 32 GW today to 57 GW by 2030. The article notes grid congestion spreading across the US, Europe and Asia-Pacific, with data-centre construction outpacing grid planning in several Asian markets.
quote: the data centre capacity in Asia-Pacific is expected to nearly double from 32GW today to 57GW by 2030
analysis: A near-doubling of regional capacity means a large Asian backup and prime-power market that competes with the Gulf for genset supply but confirms the growth thesis Cummins Arabia is selling. Action: use the JLL growth figure in data-centre pitch material as third-party evidence of demand.

title: Fitch unit BMI: grid capacity limits across Asia are binding as AI and data-centre demand rises
description: BMI, a Fitch research unit, raised its 10-year electricity consumption forecasts for Thailand (2.9%), Malaysia (3.3%) and Vietnam (5.6%) a year, mainly on data-centre investment and AI workloads. It said regulatory tightening in Thailand, Malaysia and Australia is limiting grid-connected load growth and expects a resurgence in thermal power.
quote: Grid capacity constraints across Asia are becoming increasingly binding as rising electricity demand from artificial intelligence (AI) and data centres puts pressure on power systems
analysis: Where grids cannot connect data centres quickly, regulators and developers lean on dispatchable thermal capacity, which favours on-site gas and diesel power suppliers. Action: reference the Asian grid-limit pattern when pitching on-site prime and backup power for Gulf campuses.

title: TrendForce: global data-centre power demand to reach 161 GW in 2026, up 31%, with a 268 GW grid supply gap by 2030
description: TrendForce estimates global data-centre power demand capacity at 161 GW in 2026, up about 31% year on year, and 490.7 GW by 2030 against only 222.6 GW of grid capacity available to data centres. It notes the 268 GW gap excludes behind-the-meter on-site generation, so the real shortage may be smaller.
quote: TrendForce estimates that global data center power demand capacity will reach 161 GW in 2026, up approximately 31% YoY.
analysis: The 268 GW gap is TrendForce's own estimate, but the page itself says on-site generation could offset part of it, which supports demand for gensets as grid delays persist. Action: cite the TrendForce 161 GW and 268 GW figures, labelled as TrendForce estimates, in data-centre pitch material.

title: Amsterdam data-centre vacancy falls to 2.7% as grid connection moratorium freezes new capacity until about 2029
description: Datacentres.com Research reports Amsterdam vacancy at 2.7%, the tightest in Europe, with 1,340 MW live. It says TenneT's queue shows roughly 4.6 GW of unmet demand with no headroom until new 380kV infrastructure around 2029.
quote: TenneT's transmission queue showing roughly 4.6 GW of unmet demand against zero available headroom until new 380kV infrastructure completes around 2029
analysis: Grid access, not demand, is the limiting factor in a mature hub, per Datacentres.com Research (figures not independently verified). Action: where Gulf utility connection dates slip, offer bridging or prime power in data-centre bids and confirm the connection timeline with the utility first.

title: New York/New Jersey: diesel backup faces stricter NYC air permitting as operators turn to gas turbines and fuel cells for new builds
description: Datacentres.com Research reports about 1,120 MW live in the New York/New Jersey market, with PSE&G interconnection study-to-energisation times of 42-54 months for projects above 50 MW. It says diesel backup faces stricter NYC air permitting, pushing some operators toward behind-the-meter gas turbines or fuel cells.
quote: Diesel backup generation, long the default resiliency layer for Manhattan facilities, faces increasingly restrictive New York City Department of Environmental Protection air permitting
analysis: Air-permit limits on diesel in dense US metros are steering some new builds to turbines and fuel cells, a substitution risk for diesel gensets that the page ties to NYC, not to the Gulf. Action: keep gas and dual-fuel genset options ready in Cummins Arabia data-centre offers in case Gulf permitting follows.

title: Hitachi and Bloom Energy team up on fuel-cell on-site power for data centres and industry in Japan
description: Hitachi announced a collaboration with Bloom Energy to deliver fuel-cell-based on-site power for data centres and industrial customers in Japan. Hitachi will lead planning, design and operational support and Bloom will supply the fuel cells.
quote: Hitachi will accelerate the deployment of on-site power solutions for data centers and industrial facilities by combining its control and system integration capabilities with Bloom Energy's fuel cell technology.
analysis: A large systems integrator is packaging fuel cells as on-site data-centre power, a non-genset alternative backed by an established industrial channel. Action: track whether Hitachi or Bloom offer fuel-cell packages to Gulf data-centre developers and prepare a genset-versus-fuel-cell comparison.

title: BloombergNEF: announced expansions lift global gas turbine output by more than half to 102 GW by 2030, delivery times lengthening
description: BloombergNEF's database of 44 assembly facilities at 26 manufacturers shows announced expansions lifting annual gas turbine output by more than half by 2030, to 102 GW. GE Vernova, Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries hold about 66% of capacity and supply 28 GW of the 35 GW added, almost all from expansions at existing plants.
quote: Strong demand has stretched gas turbine manufacturing capacity globally, lengthening delivery times for advanced machines.
analysis: The page says turbine delivery times are lengthening because assembly capacity is stretched and added capacity arrives only through 2030. Our reading (the page covers turbines only, not gensets): Gulf power and data-centre buyers who cannot wait for turbines may look at engine-based genset packages, which Cummins Arabia should be ready to quote against turbine timelines. Action: add a turbine-versus-genset delivery comparison to Cummins Arabia's large-project proposals.

title: Switchgear lead times 52 to 80 weeks, large diesel gensets 90 to 110 weeks; Siemens to build $185M Georgia plant
description: IndustrialSage reports medium-voltage 15kV switchgear now takes roughly 52 to 80 weeks versus about 24 weeks before the pandemic, citing June 2026 Terrapin procurement data. It lists diesel generators above 3,000 kW at 90 to 110 weeks and notes Siemens will invest at least $185 million in a Georgia low-voltage plant, with construction starting November 2026.
quote: Medium voltage switchgear runs roughly 52 to 80 weeks in the 15kV class, against about 24 weeks before the pandemic.
analysis: The article's figures are US-market data, but they show that switchgear and transformers can gate a project even when a genset is available, and the added Siemens plant comes online only over about three years. For Cummins Arabia the practical risk is that paralleling and distribution gear, not the genset, sets the handover date on data-centre jobs. Action: order switchgear and transformers in parallel with gensets on Gulf data-centre bids, and state the lead times in the offer.

title: Wärtsilä books 282 MW US data-centre engine plant order, equipment due 2028 and full operation 2029
description: Wärtsilä secured an order for a 282 MW onsite power plant with 15 Wärtsilä 50SG engines for a US data-centre project by a major independent power producer, booked in Q3 2026. It is Wärtsilä's seventh US data-centre order and takes total capacity sold for US data centres to more than 3 GW.
quote: The Wärtsilä equipment is scheduled for delivery in 2028, and the project is expected to become fully operational in 2029.
analysis: An order booked in Q3 2026 for 2028 delivery shows how far out large engine-plant slots are already being sold. Wärtsilä is a rival in large gas-engine plants, but the release covers a US project, not the Gulf. Action: track whether Wärtsilä or other engine-plant makers name a Gulf data-centre order, and prepare Cummins Arabia's prime-power gas-genset reference sheet.

title: Wärtsilä, Schneider Electric and Stanley Consultants launch integrated 'Generator-to-Chip' data-centre power offer citing delays in critical power infrastructure
description: Wärtsilä, Schneider Electric and Stanley Consultants launched a coordinated approach that combines onsite engine generation, electrical infrastructure, automation and engineering for US data-centre developers. The release says lengthy grid interconnection timelines and delays in critical power infrastructure are slowing projects.
quote: lengthy grid interconnection timelines and delays in critical power infrastructure are slowing projects
analysis: Competitors are packaging genset, switchgear and engineering as one delivery to cut the interface delays that the release blames for slowing projects. The release is US-focused and gives no schedule saving figure. Action: assemble a Cummins Arabia genset-plus-switchgear-plus-controls package with a single delivery date for Gulf data-centre bids.

title: Hitachi Energy to invest $528 million in Mississippi plant to more than double US small and medium power transformer capacity, production from 2029
description: Hitachi Energy announced on 15 Sept 2026 a $528 million factory in Gallman, Mississippi for transformers of 10 to 160 MVA up to 230 kV, with production planned to begin in 2029. It brings the company's US manufacturing expansion commitment to around $1.5 billion; Utility Dive notes that backlogs for transformers and other grid equipment are slowing grid expansion.
quote: Backlogs for transformers and other grid equipment are slowing expansion of the power grid at a time when data centers, manufacturing and electrification are rapidly increasing demand for electricity.
analysis: Transformer supply relief from this plant arrives only from 2029, and Hitachi Energy says customer lead times still depend on specification and market conditions, so transformer waits on data-centre and utility jobs are unlikely to ease soon. The article concerns US plants and does not cover Gulf deliveries. Action: ask Cummins Arabia's transformer and switchgear partners for current Gulf lead times and quote them next to genset delivery on every large bid.

title: Copper sets record on the LME at $14,875 a tonne on 10 September and a COMEX record on 22 September as metal outside the US stays scarce
description: A Canadian Mining Report analysis says three-month LME copper hit a record $14,875 a metric ton on 10 September 2026 and COMEX copper printed a record $6.83 a pound on 22 September. It attributes the rise to scarce usable metal outside the United States, with mine output down 1.1 percent in the first half of 2026.
quote: On September 10, 2026, three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange hit a record $14,875 a metric ton.
analysis: The page is about the copper market and does not mention gensets; our inference (not stated on the page) is that record copper raises the cost of alternator windings, cable and busbar, so OEM and switchgear price increases are likely to follow. Action: add a copper-price validity clause or short quote validity (estimate: 30 days) to long-dated Cummins Arabia genset and cable offers.

title: Data-centre boom hits equipment and labour shortages: transformers take 2 to 3 years, GE Vernova quotes early-2030s turbine delivery, genset-class units booked for 2028
description: Utility Dive reports that the typical customer waits two to three years for standard power transformers and generator step-up units, and GE Vernova is quoting early-2030s delivery for a backlog above 100 GW. It also cites a Wood Mackenzie webinar speaker saying smaller generating units are less supply-constrained, with orders being booked now for 2028 delivery, and Goldman Sachs predicting only 50 to 60% of planned data-centre capacity comes online in two years.
quote: The typical customer now waits two to three years for standard power transformers — which must be custom-built — and generator step-up units, according to Fluxco
analysis: Gensets and engine plants are described as less supply-constrained than turbines and transformers but are still being sold for 2028 delivery, and Goldman Sachs expects part of the announced data-centre pipeline to slip or be cancelled. The article is about the US, so the Gulf read-across is our inference. Action: for each Gulf data-centre prospect, confirm the grid-connection and transformer dates before committing Cummins Arabia genset slots, so reserved capacity is not tied to projects that slip.

title: Wood Mackenzie: 4-hour battery storage now cheaper than gas peakers worldwide; gas turbine shortages pushing up peaking costs, Middle East storage seen displacing gas peaking by 2035
description: A Wood Mackenzie analysis reported by Utility Dive says four-hour storage is cheaper than gas peakers in markets across the globe, and that in North America gas generation investment is entering a supply deficit cycle through the late 2030s. For the Middle East and Africa it forecasts four-hour storage falling 33% to $80/MWh by 2035, displacing gas peaking on cost across every gas market in the region.
quote: Gas turbine shortages and rising fuel volatility are driving up peaking costs, while expanding battery manufacturing continues to push storage costs down.
analysis: The report puts a cost edge on batteries over gas peaking in the Middle East and Africa by 2035, and names Saudi Arabia and the UAE as the lowest-cost solar markets, so battery-plus-solar hybrids may increasingly be specified instead of gas peaking plants. The 2035 timing and the peaker (not standby genset) scope mean the near-term effect on backup and prime diesel and gas gensets is limited. Action: build a genset-plus-battery hybrid offer for Gulf data-centre and industrial clients so Cummins Arabia is in the spec if storage is added.

title: US Energy Dept orders PJM to use data-centre and other backup generators as a last resort, 13-16 Oct
description: Energy Secretary Chris Wright issued an emergency order for the PJM grid (mid-Atlantic) ahead of high demand and planned generator outages. It authorises PJM to direct backup generation to run as a last resort before or during an Energy Emergency Alert 3, and DOE says over 35 GW of unused backup generation exists nationwide.
quote: authorizes PJM to direct backup generation resources to operate as a last resort before declaring an Energy Emergency Alert (EEA) 3 or during an EEA 3.
analysis: A major grid operator is now allowed to call on customer-owned backup gensets, which makes remote start, paralleling and emissions-compliant run hours part of what large buyers will ask for in standby packages. Action: brief the data-centre sales team on Cummins grid-support / demand-response genset controls so Gulf hyperscaler bids can answer the same question.

title: Malaysia asks telcos to cut diesel genset reliance at about 60,000 towers
description: On 28 September Malaysia's Communications Minister told telecom operators to reassess their dependence on diesel gensets at some 60,000 towers, especially in rural areas, and to move towards renewables under the National Energy Transition Roadmap. The government is convening partners to build a cooperation framework and possible incentives.
quote: The government has called on telecommunications companies to reassess their reliance on diesel generator sets (gensets) to operate some 60,000 telecommunication towers nationwide, particularly in rural areas.
analysis: Telecom is a long-tail genset market and a government is now pushing it towards solar-battery hybrids, which is the direction GCC telcos could also take for remote sites. The page is about Malaysia only and gives no Gulf data. Action: ask Cummins Arabia's telecom accounts whether any tower or remote-site hybrid pilots are planned and whether Cummins has a battery-hybrid offer ready.

title: Ivanhoe: hybrid solar-battery plant at Kamoa-Kakula cuts diesel generator use by about 40% in September
description: Ivanhoe Mines reported that the on-site hybrid solar facility with battery storage at Kamoa-Kakula (DRC) delivers 60 MW continuously over 24 hours and led to roughly a 40% fall in diesel generator consumption in September. The company plans to double the site's solar capacity within 18 months.
quote: Kamoa-Kakula’s on-site hybrid solar facility with battery storage led to a 40% decrease in diesel generator consumption of about 40% in September.
analysis: A large mine is showing that solar plus battery can take a big share of run hours from diesel gensets, which shrinks prime-power fuel and service revenue per site while keeping gensets as firm backup. Action: when quoting Gulf mining or remote-site power (for example in KSA), position gensets as the firming layer in hybrid designs and price the service contract on reduced run hours.

title: Bangkok halts new data-centre approvals and new licences for emergency diesel fuel storage
description: On 2 September the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration and Thailand's Energy Ministry suspended approvals for new data centres in the capital and stopped issuing new licences for diesel storage that feeds emergency backup generators. The pause stays until a Data Centre Board sets criteria on water, electricity and environmental impact; the existing storage ceiling is 500,000 litres.
quote: Both the Ministry of Energy and the BMA confirmed that all new licences for emergency fuel storage for data centres have already been suspended.
analysis: Cities are starting to regulate the on-site diesel stock that sits behind data-centre standby gensets, not just the engines, which can cap run time or force gas or battery alternatives. The page covers Bangkok only; no GCC authority is mentioned. Action: confirm fuel-storage limits in current UAE and KSA data-centre permit conditions so Cummins Arabia bids size day-tanks and run-time correctly.

title: POWER conference: federal approach lets data centres meet grid-emergency limits by switching to backup generation
description: At Data Center POWER eXchange 2026 in Washington, former White House energy adviser Peter Lake urged developers to accept flexible interconnection, cutting grid withdrawals during emergencies in return for faster connection. He said the federal requirement does not prescribe how, and options include running backup generation, pausing workloads or shifting them between sites.
quote: A facility could switch to backup generation, pause suitable computing workloads, or shift workloads among a network of data centers
analysis: Flexible-connection rules give on-site gensets a second job (grid-emergency capacity) alongside standby, which supports larger and better-controlled genset plants at data centres. The statement is a US policy view from one speaker, not a Gulf rule. Action: ask Gulf utilities (SEC, DEWA, EWEC) whether similar flexible-connection terms are planned, and prepare a genset-plus-controls offer for them.

title: Victoria (Australia) tells new data centres to supply their own renewable energy and storage
description: The Australian state of Victoria announced a regulatory framework on 22 September under which new data-centre operators must provide their own renewable supply and storage, match added demand with new generation, and cover connection costs and network upgrades. Enerdata's summary of the state statement is dated 23 September.
quote: data centre operators will first be required to provide their own renewable energy supply and storage
analysis: Rules that push data centres towards on-site renewables plus storage point to battery-plus-genset designs where gensets cover firm capacity and outages; the page does not mention gensets, so this is our reading. The rule is Australian and does not bind GCC projects. Action: ask hyperscale clients in KSA and UAE whether their global design standards are moving towards storage-led backup, and have a genset-with-battery option ready.

title: Data-centre developers are buying gas engines 'in record numbers' as gas-turbine slots run to 2032
description: POWER reports that US data-centre developers face gas-turbine delivery dates as late as 2032 and are hedging by buying gas engines, fuel cells, batteries and renewables, while Applied Digital ordered 1.2 GW of steam turbines fed by gas-fired boilers. The article cites Siemens Energy, Solar Turbines and Mitsubishi Power as reporting similar supply delays.
quote: They are also hedging their bets—purchasing gas engines, too, in record numbers as well as fuel cells, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and renewable energy.
analysis: Long turbine lead times push prime-power buyers towards reciprocating gas gensets, which is where Cummins competes with Caterpillar, Rolls-Royce mtu and Jenbacher, and the same shortage may lengthen engine and genset slots. The page is about US projects. Action: ask Cummins factory for current gas-genset slot dates and tell Gulf data-centre and industrial prospects early.

title: Aggreko US listing filing shows two data-centre contracts totalling 221 MW, about a tenth of its gas fleet
description: An Electron Economics review of Aggreko's 24 August F-1 says the prospectus discloses two recent contracts with an unnamed large US data-centre developer, 135 MW and 86 MW, totalling 221 MW. It puts Aggreko's gas generation at 2.1 GW and argues the fastest-growing contracts are long, competitively tendered ones.
quote: The prospectus also discloses two recent contracts with a large American data-center developer, which it does not name.
analysis: Power-rental firms are putting large gas fleets behind data-centre bridge power, a business that competes with owning gensets and that also buys engines from OEMs. This is a secondary newsletter review of the filing (the SEC filing itself was not opened) and covers US contracts only. Action: check how Aggreko's Gulf rental offer and pricing compare with Cummins Arabia's rental and bridge-power proposals.
